transcript:
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
is hailing the courage of the pilot of that fly Dubai flight.
He was stabbed Wednesday by another pilot.
>> In an act of unbelievable courage, he managed to unlock the door to the cockpit.
>> Unlocking the door allowed passengers to step in to subdue the attacker whose motive
remains unclear.
>> More than 170 people were on board the plane and made an emergency landing in Saudi
Arabia.
>> Tennessee Governor Bob Lee has halted executions from being carried out in the state after
a death row inmate survived two doses of a lethal injection drug.
>> In a statement, Lee said he is also ordering an outside investigation.
>> Christa Gail Pike was slated to be the first woman executed by Tennessee in at least
200 years.
>> State officials say she has been transported to an offsite medical facility.
President Trump this week again said he wants to send most American adults $5,000 checks
if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate.
And Piers Daniel Kurtzleibern reports this is just one way he has proposed increasing
the government's economic reach while railing against communism.
>> Trump's idea drew criticism from even some allies at first.
His government has also taken equity stakes in private companies, imposed dozens of tariffs
and taken the unusual step of trying to lower interest rates via the Treasury Department.
It raises a contradiction ahead of the midterms.
Trump continues to label Democrats communists and socialists, and is the leader of the party
that claims to support free markets while he tries to bend the economy to his will.
Trump's message was further muddied when he last week hosted a state dinner for Chinese
President Xi Jinping and made a friendly appearance with New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani, who
is a democratic socialist.
Daniel Kurtzleibern, NPR News.
>> The case of a former Cornell University student who alleged she was drugged and gang
raped at a fraternity in 2024 is raising questions about how police should handle cases with a
traumatized victim.
Researchers say most law enforcement investigators aren't well trained on how to handle such
situations as NPR's Jacqueline Diaz reports.
>> Trauma has a way of affecting someone's brain behavior and memory.
There may be gaps in holes in an assault survivor's story to police, and that may be due in part
to how officers question them.
Dave Thompson is a certified forensic interviewer and a consultant who trains investigators
and interrogation techniques.
>> Our memories don't work like a video recorder that we can just rewind, hit play, and remember
from start to finish what happened.
>> Thompson says investigators handling these cases should be trained in trauma informed
policing so they can use that knowledge to help build trust, which has a big effect on
investigation.
Jacqueline Diaz, NPR News.
>> This is NPR News.
A year ago, a tax credit that helped lower the cost of electric vehicles went away.
NPR's Willow Rubin reports on the impact that's had on car sales.
>> People heard the EV credit was ending last July.
EV sales spiked, and after it went away, EV sales dropped, but this year, they have stabilized.
About 6% of new cars sold every month now are electric.
Meanwhile, sales of hybrid cars this year have gone up by almost 27%, according to automotive
platform Edmunds.
Sal Iqbal is the general sales manager at the Toyota franchise in Massaciqua, New York.
He has seen this with a popular minivan that Toyota now only makes as a hybrid.
>> We used to have to literally beg people to take a CNN, and now we can't keep them
on the shelf.
>> Hybrids with gas engines and battery-powered electric motors are fuel efficient, and they
often have a lower sticker price than many EVs.
Willow Rubin, NPR News.
>> Flood watches stretch from northern New Mexico and Colorado to northern Illinois and
also in central Texas to southern Oklahoma.
The remnants of Hurricane Polo are contributing to what the National Weather Service calls
a multi-day heavy rainfall event.
Out in the Pacific, Hurricane Rachel formed Wednesday, but poses no threat to land.
However, forecasters say Rachel could become a major hurricane.
In Europe, experts say Swiss glaciers are shrinking.
A new report says glaciers in Switzerland have lost more than 5% of their ice volume
due to record heat waves and low winter snowfall.
The report highlights global warming's impact on Europe.
I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.
